classification.source: Gleditsch-Ward / Correlates of War independent-state tradition as documented by CShapes 2.0
classification.description: States are coded by their constitutional position on 1 January 1900. Independent states and the documented semi-sovereign polities selected for play are selectable; colonies, protectorates, occupied and autonomous provinces are territories of their sovereign or administering power. M11b adds the Austro-Hungarian Monarchy and documented de facto or autonomous polities. M11c replaces marker-only entries with reconstructed 1900 polygons where a defensible extent exists, and records boundary provenance, confidence and uncertainty for every polity.

states.name: Austro-Hungarian Monarchy
states.description: Dual monarchy of the Austrian and Hungarian halves under a common monarch, with joint foreign, defence and finance ministries and separate parliaments and governments.
states.notes: Cisleithania (the Austrian half) and Transleithania (the Hungarian half, including Croatia-Slavonia) each had their own government; Bosnia and Herzegovina was jointly administered. There was no single unified national flag: the common civil ensign combines the Austrian red-white-red and Hungarian red-white-green with both coats of arms. Co-capital: Budapest. The map geometry covers the core modern units (Austria, Hungary, Czechia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina); Galicia, Transylvania, Vojvodina and South Tyrol are not separable at the Natural Earth 1:50m admin-0 resolution.

states.name: Kingdom of Tonga
states.description: Independent Polynesian kingdom under the 1875 constitution, in personal rule of King George Tupou II in 1900.
states.notes: Tonga was an independent kingdom on 1 January 1900 and became a British protectorate later in 1900 (Treaty of Friendship, 18 May 1900). M11c reconstructs its territory from the modern Tongan archipelago; the archipelago's extent is not disputed.

states.name: Sokoto Caliphate
states.description: Fulani-led Islamic caliphate in the central Sudan, the largest independent state in West Africa in 1900.
states.notes: De facto independent with limited international recognition; conquered by British forces in 1903. M11c reconstructs the caliphate's core from ten modern northern Nigerian states. Population is a rounded order-of-magnitude estimate.

states.name: Sultanate of Wadai
states.description: Sahelian sultanate east of Lake Chad, independent until the French conquest of 1909–1911.
states.notes: De facto independent with limited international recognition. M11c reconstructs the sultanate's core from modern Chadian regions; the northern Tibesti and southern tributary zones are excluded. No standardised national flag design could be established; the documented monogram fallback is retained. Population is a rounded estimate.

states.name: Sultanate of Darfur
states.description: Independent sultanate in the western Sudan, conquered by Britain only in 1916.
states.notes: De facto independent with limited international recognition; the Anglo-Egyptian condominium did not control Darfur in 1900. M11c reconstructs the sultanate from the modern Darfur states as a conservative core. No standardised national flag design could be established; the documented monogram fallback is retained. Population is a rounded estimate.

states.name: Emirate of Jabal Shammar (Ha'il)
states.description: Rashidi emirate in central Arabia, the dominant state in Najd in 1900 and a rival of the Saudis.
states.notes: De facto independent and nominally Ottoman; conquered by Ibn Saud in 1921. M11c reconstructs the emirate from Ha'il, Qassim, Riyadh, the Northern Borders and al-Jowf; Ottoman sovereignty over Najd was nominal. Population is a rounded estimate.

states.name: Cretan State
states.description: Autonomous Cretan state established in 1898 under Ottoman suzerainty and Great Power guarantee, with a Greek high commissioner.
states.notes: Internationally recognised autonomous state, not a fully independent sovereign country (the 1913 union with Greece is after the reference date). M11c separates Crete from modern Greece using the modern Crete region. The flag combines the Greek cross with a red canton and white star.
